extraction.Name: Mary Shangreau
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee and refused to accept it for some time, but finally accepted on the advice of the Superintendent who told her that if she did not take it and pay the taxes that she would lose it to pay them
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged it to pay them, and used the balance to purchase another tract of land that her sister was about to lose for taxes; mortgaged it for $2000.00 to Fred Simpson of Tuthill, So. Dak.; could not pay the taxes and interest on this land so she sold it
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Fred Simpson of Tuthill, South Dakota for $2000.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: could not keep the taxes up on her land so she mortgaged it to pay them; could not pay the taxes and interest on this land so she sold it and used the money to pay the taxes and mortgage of her father's land
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent, in fair health; has no land, no home and nothing else; no dependents currently but expects to care for aging father and mother shortly; sold land and used proceeds to pay taxes and mortgage on father's land, which was the home place; has received no aid from the Government, State or County since her patent was granted; also purchased a tract her sister was about to lose for taxes; document sworn December 4, 1928
